title: Learning from Life: Bioinspired Language Model Systems for Bioengineering
content: Language models are entering bioengineering workflows that connect molecular design, computational analysis and laboratory experiments. Their value depends on more than predictive accuracy: systems must coordinate decisions, learn from observations, retain reliable experience and execute actions under physical constraints. This critical narrative survey compares bioinspired mechanisms across collective organization, evolutionary and coevolutionary search, neurocognitive learning and consolidation, developmental self-organization, immune-inspired defense, and neuromorphic implementation. We distinguish these mechanisms from models trained on biological data and from computation performed by living or molecular substrates. Evidence spans language benchmarks, artificial-life simulations, robotics, hardware, biomolecular assays and cellular experiments. Collective methods depend on information access and communication; population search depends on variation, evaluators and retained diversity. Memory and predictive-coding studies introduce distinct learning and retention mechanisms, while developmental and immune systems remain concentrated in computational demonstrations. Neuromorphic efficiency depends on workload, encoding and whole-system accounting. Applications span proteins, functional RNA, genomic components, cellular perturbations, biomaterials and scientific laboratories. We develop a comparative mechanism map and evaluation framework connecting the adaptive object, feedback source and independent acceptance endpoint. The central priority is to identify which biological principle contributes measurable value beyond matched conventional alternatives, while preserving provenance, existing capabilities and realistic experimental budgets.
